subject: general
question: In a circuit with a NTC type thermistor and a fixed resistor connected in series connected to a DC power supply, what will happen to the output voltage if there is a rise in temperature?

options.text: The output voltage will fluctuate depending on the resistor value.
The output voltage will remain constant.

solution:
The correct answer is __The output voltage will increase**(Option 4)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• NTC thermistor__ stands for Negative Temperature Coefficient thermistor.
 
• An NTC thermistor's resistance decreases as the temperature increases.
 
• The circuit in question has an NTC thermistor and a fixed resistor in series connected to a DC power supply.
 
• When the resistance of the NTC thermistor decreases, the voltage drop across it decreases.
 
• This results in an increase in the output voltage across the fixed resistor.
 
• This behavior is consistent with the characteristics of an NTC thermistor in such a circuit configuration.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Fixed Resistor:**

 
 
• A fixed resistor is a passive component used to resist the flow of current in an electrical circuit.
 
• Its resistance value does not change with temperature or other environmental factors.
 
 
 
• **NTC Thermistor:**
 
 
• An NTC thermistor is a temperature-sensitive resistor whose resistance decreases with an increase in temperature.
 
• They are widely used in temperature measurement and control applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of NTC Thermistors:**
 
 
• Used in automotive temperature sensors.
 
• Commonly found in HVAC systems for temperature regulation.
